title: Long division: 7 divided by 12
description: Aligned place-value columns, subtraction, and bring-down arrows show why only the 3 repeats in 7/12 = 0.58[3].
transcript: Divide 7 by 12. Because 7 is less than 12, write 0 before the decimal point in the quotient. Write 7 as 7.000 and align the decimal points.
12 goes into 70 five times. Write 5 in the tenths place. Subtract 60 from 70 to get 10. Bring down the next 0 to make 100.
12 goes into 100 eight times. Write 8 in the hundredths place. Subtract 96 from 100 to get 4. Bring down another 0 to make 40.
12 goes into 40 three times. Write 3 in the thousandths place. Subtract 36 from 40 to get 4 again.
Bringing down another 0 would give 40 again, so the digit 3 and the remainder 4 repeat. Thus 7/12 = 0.58333… = 0.58[3]. The recurring bar covers only the 3.

title: Solve and check: 3x + 6 = 21
description: The work shows the same operation on both sides, aligned equality signs, and a substitution check for x = 5.
transcript: Subtract 6 from both sides: 3x + 6 − 6 = 21 − 6. Simplify to 3x = 15.
Divide both sides by 3: (3x)/3 = 15/3. Simplify to x = 5.
Check in the original equation: 3(5) + 6 = 15 + 6 = 21. This equals the original right side, so x = 5 is the solution.
